A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChessArena work and contain 36 complete, readable pages, including appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the scientific content and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original chess competitions, fine-grained evaluations and Qwen3 post-training results in Section 4, with additional experiments and analyses in appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including chess evaluations, training analyses and cross-domain benchmark results in Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: The ChessArena procedures, Glicko matchmaking, two supervised fine-tuning stages and subsequent GRPO training are unchanged. The components and reward functions in appendices B–C also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data, four chess play modes, three fine-grained evaluation tasks and cross-domain benchmarks in Appendix F.2. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same LLMs, Qwen3 training variants, Maia-1100, Random Player and Stockfish participate in their corresponding comparisons. Comparator membership is unchanged in both main-text and appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and appendices A, C and D retain identical prompts, decoding settings, training budgets and legal-move conditions. Evaluation sizes remain 200 basic-understanding instances, 1,000 move-selection instances and 1,008 puzzles.

E4.justification: The move-history experiment, Blindfold and ZebraLogic case studies, legal-move-constraint analysis, and RL training curves and rollout analyses are unchanged in appendices E–F.

E5.justification: Glicko rating deviations and 95% confidence-interval reporting in Tables 1 and 10 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run information, seed information or statistical estimation procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains ratings of 2220 for Maia-1100, 1948 for O3 and 1776 for Qwen3-8B-Chess; appendix results and training curves also match.

T1.justification: The MAR definition in Section 2.5, Glicko equations and matchmaking derivation in Appendix B, and reward definitions in Appendix C.3 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same core contributions and claims concerning ChessArena, weaknesses in current LLM chess reasoning, and improvements from Qwen3 chess post-training. The added code link does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of Blindfold failures, legal-move dependence and cross-domain transfer remain identical. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning outcome-supervision noise and possible reliance on memorization.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit GitHub link to NEU-CS/ChessArena at the end of the abstract; v1 contains no corresponding project-code link. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters and hardware descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including Section 5's comparisons with chess language models and GameArena. The bibliography is identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short code-access statement to the abstract and updates the title-page and arXiv version dates. Scientific wording, terminology and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract text produces limited text reflow and spacing changes: the Bullet description moves from page 2 to page 3, and the Discussion heading from page 8 to page 9. Figures and tables retain their displays; appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The new abstract code link supplies a concrete implementation access point missing from v1, modestly improving reproducibility information. Scientific evidence and appendices remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked repository's contents or completeness.
